items.text: Given: A is a point outside the circle M, AB and AC are two tangent segments of the circle at B and C. R.T.P: Prove that: AB = AC. onstruction: Draw MB, MC and MA.

items.text: Proof: ∵ AB is a tangent segment to circle M ∴ m(∠ABM) = 90°. ∵ AC is a tangent segment to circle M ∴ m(∠ACM) = 90°.

items.claim: The straight line passing through the center of the circle and the intersection point of the two tangents is an axis of symmetry to the chord of tangency of those two tangents.

items.quote: The straight line passing through the center of the circle and
items.claim: The straight line passing through the center of the circle and the intersection point of its two tangents bisects the angle between these two tangents. It also bisects the angle between the two radii passing through the two points of tangency.

items.quote: In the opposite figure : XA and XB are two tangents
items.stem: In the opposite figure: $\overrightarrow{XA}$ and $\overrightarrow{XB}$ are two tangents to the circle at A and B. $m(\angle AXB)=70^\circ$, $m(\angle DCB)=125^\circ$. Prove that: First: $\overrightarrow{AB}$ bisects $\angle DAX$. Second: $\overrightarrow{AD}\parallel\overrightarrow{XB}$.
solution: Given: $\overrightarrow{XA}$ and $\overrightarrow{XB}$ are two tangents to the circle, $m(\angle AXB)=70^\circ$ and $m(\angle DCB)=125^\circ$.
Proof: ∵ XA and XB are two tangent segments ∴ XA = XB
∵ ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, $m(\angle C)=125^\circ$
From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle XAB)=m(\angle DAB)=55^\circ$
items.notes: Proof printed with step labels (1) and (2) and reason annotations.

items.claim: The inscribed circle of a polygon is the circle which touches all of its sides internally.

items.text: M is the inscribed circle of the triangle ABC because it touches all of its sides internally at D, E and F. i.e.: The triangle ABC is drawn outside the circle M.

items.quote: M is an inscribed circle to the quadrilateral ABCD with radius
items.stem: In the opposite figure: M is an inscribed circle to the quadrilateral ABCD with radius length of 5 cm. AB = 9 cm and CD = 12 cm. Find the perimeter of ABCD, then calculate its area.
solution: ∵ The circle M is an inscribed circle to the quadrilateral ABCD
∴ The circle M touches the sides of ABCD at X, Y, Z and L
∵ $\overline{AX}$ and $\overline{AL}$ are two tangent segments to the circle M

items.quote: In the opposite figure :
items.caption: Quadrilateral ABCD with inscribed circle M (blue) touching AD at L, AB at X, CB at Y, CD at Z. Radius R drawn from M to Y. Dashed lines from M to vertices. Read from figure; verify.
solution: ∵ BX and BY are two tangent segments to circle M ∴ BX = BY
By addition, we get: (AX + BX) + (CZ + DZ) = AL + BY + CY + DL
∴ AB + CD = AD + BC = 1/2 the perimeter of ABCD
Area of ABCD = 1/2 AB × r + 1/2 BC × r + 1/2 CD × r + 1/2 AD × r

learning_objectives.label: Tangent segments from a point outside a circle
learning_objectives.description: Use the equality of the two tangent segments drawn to a circle from a point outside it, and the corollaries (the line through the centre and the intersection point of the tangents is the axis of the chord of tangency and bisects the angle between the tangents), to find unknown lengths and angle measures and to prove relations.

learning_objectives.label: Circle inscribed in a polygon
learning_objectives.description: Use the circle inscribed in a polygon (touching all of its sides internally) and equal tangent segments to find the perimeter and area of the polygon and the position of the centre.

learning_objectives.label: Common tangents of two circles
learning_objectives.description: Distinguish common internal and common external tangents of two circles, and solve problems finding unknown values and the length of a common tangent.
